_rules: This file is the only place a facility, bill or system name is defined. Pages are built from it by scripts/build.mjs.

Facility names: the official name is the tag. Local and record names go in aliases. Never add a second facility for a place already listed; add an alias instead. The build refuses an alias that matches another facility's name or alias.
Bills: LD numbers restart every Legislature, so a bill's id is <legislature>-<LD>, e.g. 132-1962.
System is who holds the person: county, state, federal, juvenile, supervision, or multiple when the piece is about the handoff between them.
Facilities outside Maine are listed only when a record shows people from Maine are held there. Put that record in maine_tie.
Topic answers what the story is about. Every item gets exactly one. If two topics fit, pick the one the headline is about; if that is a coin flip, note it in topic_note so the list can be redrawn.
Format answers what kind of piece it is: news, investigation, data, explainer or document.

To publish issue N: copy src/issues/<N-1>.html to src/issues/N.html and edit it (entry ids, /issue/N permalinks, filed markers), add data.issues[N] with its publication date, and add each entry to items with issue N and url /issue/N#<id>. The build writes /issue/N and makes it the home page; earlier issues stay at their own addresses.

items.topic_note: Coin flip with Conditions and Safety: the story is a new jail, filed under the bond and site cost.
items.title: Eight properties are in the running for the county’s next jail
items.summary: Land proposals for Aroostook County’s next jail were due Sept. 28. Eight were submitted: three in Caribou, two in Houlton, and one each in Presque Isle, Limestone and Fort Fairfield.

items.title: Corrections keeps the rule allowing sanctions regardless of a hearing’s outcome
items.summary: In its response to public comments on its adult resident discipline rule, the Maine Department of Corrections said Procedure O.21 “will not be removed.”

items.title: State prisons held 2,100 people on an average day in August
items.summary: The Department of Corrections’ August report puts the average incarcerated population at 2,100: 1,884 men and 215 women.

items.title: Corrections’ rules on legislator access to facilities are due
items.summary: LD 1962 requires the Corrections commissioner to adopt rules setting which areas legislators may enter, how they may speak with residents and staff, and when entry may be refused.

items.topic_note: Also covers money (deficit, design firm) and courts (pretrial waits).
items.title: Aroostook County Jail: perfect scores, unsafe building
items.summary: Five straight 100 percent state inspections. No fire suppression. A capacity that rose as the jail filled, a deficit that tripled, a death the record barely notes, and a design firm the county’s own interview team did not pick.

items.topic_note: Coin flip with Conditions and Safety: deaths and inspections versus the care policy in the headline.
items.title: FCC Petersburg: transgender people in federal custody
items.summary: Three people died at the complex in six weeks this spring, and the Bureau of Prisons has not said how. The only public count of transgender people held there, 61 in 2023, predates a care policy that has since been rewritten, blocked and rewritten again.

items.topic_note: Coin flip with Law and Policy: incidents and audits versus jail oversight.

items.summary: What the Department of Corrections’ staff newsletter recorded about the women held at Windham and about Aroostook County Jail, issue by issue, with the dates to cite in a records request.
